### WRITE SOME HELPER FUNCTIONS TO MAKE COMPARISON LIST AND SPECIES THRESHOLDS 
```{r helper-functions,include=TRUE}
# HELPER FUNCTIONS  -------------------------------------------------------
merge_by_rownames <- function(x,y) {
  merge <- merge(x,y,by='row.names')
  rownames(merge) <- merge$Row.names
  merge[,!colnames(merge) %in% c('Row.names')]
}

## FUNCTION TO MAKE THE COMPARISON LIST 
dir <- './HmscOutputs'
pattern <- '2026-02-10'
get_preds <- function(dir,pattern){
  pattern2match <- pattern
  
  matching_folders <- list.dirs(dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = F)
  matching_folders <- matching_folders[grepl(pattern2match,
                                             basename(matching_folders))]
  model <- matching_folders[1]
  models_nums <- as.numeric(str_extract(matching_folders, "(?<=Atlas)\\d+"))
  
  outputs <- lapply(matching_folders,function(model){
    # read objects
    load(file.path(dir,model,'Models','Fitted','HPC_samples_0250_thin_100_chains_4.Rdata'))
    m <- fitted_model$posteriors
    preds <- pcomputePredictedValues(m)
    
    # 1. Flatten the list and reshape it into a 3D array (sites x species x samples)
    # unlist() is incredibly fast compared to binding functions

    # 2. Calculate the mean across the 3rd dimension (the samples)
    # dims = 2 tells R to keep the first two dimensions and average across the rest
    EpredY <- rowMeans(preds, dims = 2)
    empirical <- m$Y
    comparison_list <- list(predictions = EpredY,
                            empirical = empirical)
    
    saveRDS(comparison_list,
            file=file.path(dir,model,'Tests','comparisonlist.RData'))
  })
}

# FUNCTION TO LOAD THE COMPARISON LIST AND GET SPECIES-THRESHOLDS BASED ON DIFFERENT METRICS 
dir <- './HmscOutputs'
pattern <- '2026-02-10'

get_thresholds <- function(dir,pattern,methods){
  
  pattern2match <- pattern # get pattern 
  matching_folders <- list.dirs(dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = F) # get dirs 
  matching_folders <- matching_folders[grepl(pattern2match,
                                             basename(matching_folders))] # get folders
  model <- matching_folders[1]
  models_nums <- as.numeric(str_extract(matching_folders, "(?<=Atlas)\\d+")) # get atlas
  
  ### LOOP OVER DIFFERENT MODELS 
  lapply(matching_folders,function(model){ 
    # READ OBJECTS 
    readRDS(file.path(dir,model,'Tests','comparisonlist.Rdata'))
    method <- methods[[1]]
    
    ### LOOP OVER DIFFERENT OPTIMIZATION THRESHOLDS 
    vects <- lapply(methods,function(method){
      threshold_vect <- get_species_thresholds(preds = comparison_list$predictions,
                                               obs = comparison_list$empirical,
                                               method = method)
      return(threshold_vect)
    })
    
    names(vects) <- methods
    saveRDS(vects,
            file = file.path(dir,model,'Tests','optimized-species-thresholds.Rdata'))
  })
}
get_species_thresholds <- function(preds, obs, method = "MaxSens+Spec") {
  # Create a named vector to store results
  thresh_vector <- setNames(numeric(ncol(preds)), colnames(preds))
  
  sp <- colnames(preds)[[1]]
  for (sp in colnames(preds)) {
    # PresenceAbsence package requires a specific data frame format:
    # Col 1: Site ID, Col 2: Observed (0/1), Col 3: Predicted probability
    data_prep <- data.frame(
      ID = 1:nrow(preds), 
      obs = obs[, sp], 
      pred = preds[, sp]
    )
    
    # optimal.thresholds returns a data frame; we pull the second column (the value)
    # Common methods: "MaxSens+Spec", "Sens=Spec", "ObsPrev"
    opt <- optimal.thresholds(data_prep, opt.methods = method)
    thresh_vector[sp] <- opt[1, 2]
  }
  
  return(thresh_vector)
}
```

```{r functions-for-visualising}
dir <- './HmscOutputs'
pattern <- '2026-02-10'

make_richness_jaccard_df <- function(dir,pattern){
  
  pattern2match <- pattern # get pattern 
  matching_folders <- list.dirs(dir, recursive = FALSE, full.names = F) # get dirs 
  matching_folders <- matching_folders[grepl(pattern2match,
                                             basename(matching_folders))] # get folders
  model_folder <- matching_folders[1]
  models_nums <- as.numeric(str_extract(matching_folders, "(?<=Atlas)\\d+")) # get atlas
  
  # Helper to make threshold names "clean" for column headers
  clean_name <- function(x) {
    x <- gsub("\\+", "_plus_", x)
    x <- gsub("=", "_equal_", x)
    return(tolower(x))
  }
  # Helper function for Jaccard Similarity
  calc_jaccard <- function(m1, m2) {
    intersect <- rowSums((m1 == 1) & (m2 == 1))
    union <- rowSums((m1 == 1) | (m2 == 1))
    return(ifelse(union == 0, 1, intersect / union))
  }
  ### LOOP OVER DIFFERENT MODELS (Inside your make_richness_jaccard_df function)
  all_results <- lapply(matching_folders, function(model_folder) {
    
    cat("Processing:", model_folder, "\n")
    
    # READ OBJECTS 
    comparison <- readRDS(file.path(dir, model_folder, 'Tests', 'comparisonlist.Rdata'))
    thresholds <- readRDS(file.path(dir, model_folder, 'Tests', 'optimized-species-thresholds.Rdata'))
    load(file.path(dir,model_folder,'Models','Fitted','HPC_samples_0250_thin_100_chains_4.Rdata'))
    m <- fitted_model$posteriors
    xycoords <- m$ranLevels$site$s
    
    # Extract matrices for readability
    pred_mat <- comparison$predictions
    emp_mat <- comparison$empirical

        # Ensure site_meta is built from the exact rows we are analyzing
    site_meta <- data.frame(full_id = rownames(pred_mat), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      separate(full_id, into = c("site", "atlas"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
      left_join(
        xycoords %>%
          rownames_to_column("site"),
        by = "site"
        )
    
    # --- FIX 1: MATCH BY ROWNAME FOR EMPIRICAL RICHNESS ---
    # We extract the rows from emp_mat in the exact order of pred_mat's rownames
    emp_aligned <- emp_mat[site_meta$full_id, , drop = FALSE]
    
    res_df <- site_meta %>%
      mutate(
        folder = model_folder,
        rich_empirical = rowSums(emp_aligned)
      )
    
    # 2. Loop through the three threshold types
    for (t_name in names(thresholds)) {
      
      thresh_vals <- thresholds[[t_name]]
      
      # --- FIX 2: MATCH BY SPECIES NAMES FOR THRESHOLDS ---
      # We index the threshold vector using the exact column (species) names of pred_mat.
      # This guarantees that Species A's probability is tested against Species A's threshold.
      aligned_thresh <- thresh_vals[colnames(pred_mat)]
      
      # Binarize predictions: Compare each species column to its specific threshold
      bin_mat <- sweep(pred_mat, 2, aligned_thresh, ">") * 1
      
      # Calculate Richness
      rich_col_name <- paste0("rich_pred_", clean_name(t_name))
      res_df[[rich_col_name]] <- rowSums(bin_mat)
      
      # --- FIX 3: MAKE SURE ROWS & COLS ARE ALIGNED FOR JACCARD ---
      # We force the empirical matrix to match BOTH the rows and columns of the binarized matrix
      # before running the jaccard calculation.
      emp_for_jaccard <- emp_mat[rownames(bin_mat), colnames(bin_mat), drop = FALSE]
      
      jacc_col_name <- paste0("jaccard_", clean_name(t_name))
      res_df[[jacc_col_name]] <- calc_jaccard(emp_for_jaccard, bin_mat)
    }
    
    return(res_df)
})
  # Combine all folders into one master dataframe
  final_df <- bind_rows(all_results)
  return(final_df)

}

df <- make_richness_jaccard_df(dir,pattern)
atlas_idx <- 1
metric <- 'jaccard'

plot_atlas_dashboard <- function(df, atlas_idx, 
                                 rich_palette = c("blue", "white", "red"),
                                 rich_limits = c(0, 50),
                                 diff_palette = c("purple", "white", "orange"), # New
                                 diff_limits = c(-20, 20),                      # New
                                 jacc_palette = c("black", "green"),
                                 jacc_limits = c(0, 1),
                                 rel_widths = c(1.5, 1, 1),
                                 overarching_title = NULL) {
  
  # 1. Filter data
  df_sub <- df %>% filter(atlas == atlas_idx)
  
  thresh_names <- c("maxsens_plus_spec", "sens_equal_spec", "obsprev")
  thresh_labels <- c("MaxSens + Spec", "Sens = Spec", "Obs Prev")
  
  theme_map <- function() {
    theme_minimal() +
      theme(
        axis.text = element_blank(), 
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), 
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
      )
  }

  # --- Column 1: Empirical ---
  avg_emp <- mean(df_sub$rich_empirical, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_emp <- ggplot(df_sub, aes(X, Y, color = rich_empirical)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7) +
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = rich_palette, limits = rich_limits) +
    coord_fixed() + 
    labs(title = sprintf("Empirical Richness\n(Mean: %.2f)", avg_emp)) + 
    theme_map()

  # --- Column 2: Richness Difference (Pred - Emp) ---
  p_diff_list <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
    col_name <- paste0("rich_pred_", thresh_names[i])
    # Calculate difference locally for plotting
    df_sub$diff_val <- df_sub[[col_name]] - df_sub$rich_empirical
    avg_diff <- mean(df_sub$diff_val, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    ggplot(df_sub, aes(X, Y, color = diff_val)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.5) +
      scale_color_gradientn(colors = diff_palette, limits = diff_limits) +
      coord_fixed() + 
      labs(title = sprintf("Richness difference: %s\n(Mean difference: %.2f)", thresh_labels[i], avg_diff)) +
      theme_map()
  })

  # --- Column 3: Jaccard ---
  p_jacc_list <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
    col_name <- paste0("jaccard_", thresh_names[i])
    avg <- mean(df_sub[[col_name]], na.rm = TRUE)
    ggplot(df_sub, aes(X, Y, color = .data[[col_name]])) +
      geom_point(size = 0.5) +
      scale_color_gradientn(colors = jacc_palette, limits = jacc_limits) +
      coord_fixed() + 
      labs(title = sprintf("Jaccard similarity: %s\n(Mean: %.2f)", thresh_labels[i], avg)) +
      theme_map()
  })

  # 3. LEGEND EXTRACTION
  # Richness Legend
  p_leg_rich <- p_emp + 
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") + 
    guides(color = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)) +
    labs(color = "Species Richness")
  leg_rich <- get_legend(p_leg_rich)
    
  # Difference Legend (Extracted from a dummy plot)
  tmp_diff <- ggplot(df_sub, aes(X, Y, color = rich_empirical)) + 
    geom_point() + 
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = diff_palette, limits = diff_limits, name = "Richness difference (Pred-Obs)") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    guides(color = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
  leg_diff <- get_legend(tmp_diff)
  
  # Jaccard Legend
  tmp_jacc <- ggplot(df_sub, aes(X, Y, color = jaccard_obsprev)) +
    geom_point() + 
    scale_color_gradientn(colors = jacc_palette, limits = jacc_limits, name = "Jaccard similarity") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    guides(color = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)) 
  leg_jacc <- get_legend(tmp_jacc)

  # 4. ASSEMBLY
  col2 <- plot_grid(plotlist = p_diff_list, ncol = 1)
  col3 <- plot_grid(plotlist = p_jacc_list, ncol = 1)
 top_row <- plot_grid(p_emp, col2, col3, ncol = 3, rel_widths = rel_widths)
  
  # Legend Row with 3 legends
  legend_row <- plot_grid(leg_rich, leg_diff, leg_jacc, ncol = 3)
  
  # 5. TITLE & FINAL STACK
  if (is.null(overarching_title)) overarching_title <- paste("Atlas Analysis:", atlas_idx)
  title_label <- ggdraw() + draw_label(overarching_title, fontface = 'bold', size = 14)

  final_dash <- plot_grid(
    title_label, 
    top_row, 
    legend_row, 
    ncol = 1, 
    rel_heights = c(0.1, 1, 0.15) # Adjusted for 3 legends
  )

  return(final_dash)
}

### MAKE SUMMARY DATAFRAME
create_global_summary_table <- function(df) {
  
  # 1. Define the threshold names and labels as they appear in your data
  thresh_lookup <- data.frame(
    suffix = c("maxsens_plus_spec", "sens_equal_spec", "obsprev"),
    Label = c("MaxSens + Spec", "Sens = Spec", "Obs Prev")
  )
  
  # 2. Iterate through each unique Atlas
  summary_list <- lapply(unique(df$atlas), function(a_idx) {
    df_sub <- df %>% filter(atlas == a_idx)
    
    # Calculate empirical mean once per atlas
    avg_emp <- mean(df_sub$rich_empirical, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Calculate metrics for each threshold
    lapply(1:nrow(thresh_lookup), function(i) {
      suff <- thresh_lookup$suffix[i]
      
      pred_col <- paste0("rich_pred_", suff)
      jacc_col <- paste0("jaccard_", suff)
      
      # Calculations
      avg_pred <- mean(df_sub[[pred_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      avg_diff <- mean(df_sub[[pred_col]] - df_sub$rich_empirical, na.rm = TRUE)
      avg_jacc <- mean(df_sub[[jacc_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
      
      # Return a single row for this Atlas/Threshold combination
      data.frame(
        Atlas = a_idx,
        Threshold = thresh_lookup$Label[i],
        `Empirical Rich.` = round(avg_emp, 2),
        `Pred. Rich.` = round(avg_pred, 2),
        `Mean Bias` = round(avg_diff, 2),
        `Mean Jaccard` = round(avg_jacc, 2),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }) %>% bind_rows()
  }) %>% bind_rows()
  
  # 3. Format as a Kable Table
  # We use 'collapse_rows' logic so Atlas names only appear once per group
  return(knitr::kable(summary_list, 
                      format = "markdown", 
                      caption = "Summary Metrics of Community Prediction Performance across Atlases"))
}
```
